value.rationale: An exact, globally optimized worst-case two-erasure stability law for a natural quadrature-weighted Chebyshev sampling scheme provides finite-N condition numbers for any lost pair and proves a fifth-power noise-amplification boundary. The difference from the previously studied half-shifted Gauss seventh-power law is structurally motivated by the geometry of endpoint nodes, not a mere renaming or known-table recomputation. The theorem includes a complete frequency-restricted singular spectrum and a unique geometric extremizer classification.
